 Walmart's flywheel seems to be gathering steam.
 The retail giant posted another quarter of strong sales growth on Thursday, with total revenue of $188.8 billion for the quarter, up 5.2% over last year and ahead of analyst expectations.
 In the US division, comparable sales were up 2.9%, led by growth in grocery and increased visits from higher-income shoppers . The company said new laws about pharmaceutical pricing took about a percentage point off its comparable sales performance.
 US e-commerce grew 23% for the quarter, with more than four out of every five online orders fulfilled from stores, including some third-party marketplace items. Delivery is getting faster, too, as a larger share of orders were fulfilled in less than three hours.
 And at the company's warehouse chain, Sam's Club, fuel accounted for nearly half of the quarter's 9.7% sales growth as high gas prices during the quarter stretched household budgets.
 The company's earnings call starts at 8 a.m. Eastern Time.

 Dominick Reuter is a senior retail reporter for Business Insider, primarily covering Walmart, Target, Costco, and other big box retailers. His stories tend to focus on issues and trends that affect employees and customers, such as affordability challenges and the growing race to provide ultra-fast delivery services on e-commerce orders. Prior to joining BI in 2019, Dominick worked for more than a decade as an independent photojournalist covering a wide range of stories for global wire services and newspapers, including Reuters, the Wall Street Journal, and Agence France-Presse. Dominick studied photojournalism at Boston University and later earned a Masters in business and economics journalism from Columbia University.
